content.value_statement: Browser storage workflows can fail when buckets, domains, or access rules are incomplete. This skill guides CloudBase Web SDK uploads, downloads, temporary URLs, and environment checks.
actual_capabilities: Shows when to use CloudBase Web SDK storage methods for browser apps.
Explains upload, temporary URL, delete, and download flows.
Distinguishes PG storage buckets from legacy CloudBase storage paths.
Describes security-domain checks for local and hosted browser origins.
Provides error-handling guidance for missing buckets and failed uploads.
limitations: It does not replace CloudBase product documentation or console permissions.
It does not create buckets, domains, or RLS policies by itself.
It focuses on browser-side storage, not backend batch storage management.
It assumes the user can access the correct CloudBase environment.

use_cases.title: Add Browser Uploads
use_cases.description: Implement a Web SDK upload flow that stores files and returns a usable preview URL.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Storage Setup
use_cases.description: Check missing buckets, security domains, and upload errors before changing application code.

use_cases.title: Plan PG Storage Access
use_cases.description: Configure PG storage bucket usage and RLS expectations for authenticated browser users.

prompt_templates.title: Upload A File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use CloudBase Web SDK to upload a selected browser file. Include the setup checks I need before testing.

prompt_templates.title: Preview An Uploaded File
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a CloudBase browser upload flow that resolves a temporary preview URL after the upload succeeds.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Upload Failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose my CloudBase Web SDK upload failure. Check bucket existence, security domains, and the correct API for my storage mode.

prompt_templates.title: Design PG Storage Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a CloudBase PG storage browser workflow with bucket naming, authenticated uploads, signed URLs, and RLS policy considerations.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a profile image upload flow in a CloudBase browser app.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the upload method, validates file size and type, resolves a temporary URL, and handles upload failure clearly.

output_examples.input: A local development upload fails with a CORS or domain error.
output_examples.output: The response checks the actual browser origin, compares it with CloudBase security domains, and recommends adding the exact host and port.

output_examples.input: A PG storage upload reports that the bucket is missing.
output_examples.output: The response explains that the bucket must exist first and separates PG bucket names from legacy path prefixes.

best_practices: Confirm the storage bucket and browser security domain before testing uploads.
Use temporary URLs instead of constructing public links by hand.
Reject the parent workflow when an upload fails.
anti_patterns: Do not fabricate a file URL after a failed upload.
Do not use legacy NoSQL upload methods for PG storage buckets.
Do not assume a fixed local development port is already trusted.

faq.question: Does this skill upload files by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides code and setup decisions for CloudBase Web SDK storage flows.

faq.question: Is this for browser code or backend code?
faq.answer: It is for browser-side CloudBase Web SDK storage operations.

faq.question: Can it help with temporary download links?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when to use temporary URLs and how to handle missing URL results.

faq.question: Does it cover CloudBase PG storage?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains bucket naming, signed URLs, and RLS requirements for PG storage.

faq.question: Can it solve CORS problems?
faq.answer: It helps identify security-domain requirements, but the CloudBase environment must be updated separately.

faq.question: Should agents use this for static hosting?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly separates storage objects from static website hosting deployment.
